prg_main.title: Representation Transfer via Invariant Input-driven Continuous Attractors for Fast Domain Adaptation

source_extracted_configuration.rnn: Three separately pretrained vanilla RNNs, 512 neurons each, tau=2 time steps, leaky ReLU recurrence plus per-time-step layer normalization; truncated BPTT with Adam lr=1e-4; paper says convergence within 1e6 training episodes, about 48h on one NVIDIA A40.
source_extracted_configuration.direction_pretraining: T=100 moving-bar clips, 12 directions, sparse Bernoulli input noise p=0.01, predict motion angle.
source_extracted_configuration.velocity_pretraining: Moving bars at 5 discrete speeds x 12 directions, jointly encode speed and direction.
source_extracted_configuration.salience_pretraining: Dot-cloud clips with smoothly drifting Gaussian centroid, estimate x,y.
source_extracted_configuration.synthetic_manifold_probe: 500 clips x 100 frames covering the full motion-variable range.
source_extracted_configuration.downstream_freeze_boundary: The pretrained RNN dynamics are transferred without retraining; downstream task-specific RBF SVMs with Platt scaling and optional lightweight Hebbian fusion are trained/adapted.
source_extracted_configuration.dvs_preprocessing: ST-core binary denoising; st1 42x42 uses (DeltaST_s,theta_s,DeltaST_t,theta_t)=(3,2,3,2); st2 128x128 uses (1,1,2,2).
source_extracted_configuration.rgb_preprocessing: YOLOv8 subject crop 500x500 from 1920x1080; 10x10 and 4x4 average pooling for st1/st2; temporal difference against final frame; fixed 95% binarization threshold.
source_extracted_configuration.baselines: Inflated ResNet-50 C3D trained 30 epochs, Adam lr=1e-4, weight decay 1e-5, batch 16; ViViT factorized encoder trained 50 epochs, AdamW lr=5e-5, weight decay 1e-4, batch 8.

key_findings: Supplementary Table 1 exposes a strong downstream-adapter contribution in the lowest-data DVS regime: with 5 samples/category, Hebbian fusion is 0.697 versus 0.635 without Hebbian fusion (+6.2 percentage points). At 10/20/50 samples the gaps shrink to +2.1/+0.3/+0.1 points.
RGB macro averages do not show the same uniform Hebbian benefit: at 5/10/20/50 samples, Heb vs No-Heb is 0.723/0.723, 0.777/0.780, 0.848/0.833, 0.866/0.869.

Supplementary Fig. 4 is a stronger mechanism ablation than module-addition alone: direction-only pretraining is compared with mixed direction+position and direction+speed representations; mixed representations can perform well on synthetic pretraining but show reduced real-task flow alignment and substantially worse interpolation/frame-dropout robustness.
Supplementary Fig. 4 therefore supports representation isolation/disentanglement as a causal design factor, but the PDF does not provide machine-readable exact transfer-curve values.

adapter_contribution.interpretation: The few-shot gain cannot be attributed solely to frozen attractor representations; a lightweight task-specific fusion rule contributes materially in the most data-starved DVS setting.

mechanism_ablation.interpretation: The most mechanism-specific evidence is not merely adding more modules. Supplementary Fig. 4 shows that explicitly isolating a low-dimensional direction primitive yields markedly more robust transfer than entangling direction with position or speed, despite mixed representations retaining synthetic pretraining competence.
mechanism_ablation.scope: Exact curve coordinates are image-only in the supplement and were not numerically reconstructed; treat this as qualitative-to-semiquantitative causal evidence, not an exact effect-size estimate.

candidate_update.mechanism: Task-agnostic synthetic pretraining sculpts reusable low-dimensional input-driven continuous attractors in separate vanilla RNN modules; downstream domains reuse frozen dynamics and train lightweight adapters/fusion.
evidence_added_this_run: Direction/velocity/salience RNNs each have 512 neurons and source-defined synthetic curricula; training is substantial pretraining (up to 1e6 episodes, about 48h/A40), while downstream adaptation is light rather than the entire system being cheap to train from scratch.
Supplementary Table 1: DVS 5-shot Hebbian fusion 69.7% versus direct fusion 63.5%; the adapter explains 6.2 pp of the approximately-70% few-shot result.

Supplementary Fig. 4: mixed direction+position and direction+speed representations transfer less robustly than explicitly isolated direction representations, supporting low-dimensional disentanglement as a mechanism rather than only architecture size.
No clear independent reproduction/failure found in current public search.
scope: This is domain adaptation/action recognition over relatively rigid low-dimensional motion primitives, not general continual learning.
Frozen attractor representations are not the sole source of downstream accuracy; RBF SVM/calibration and optional Hebbian fusion are trained per downstream task.
Pretraining cost is nontrivial and should be amortized across tasks before claiming system-level efficiency.
Headline benchmark uncertainty and exact few-shot sampling/seeding remain unresolved pending code.
RGB class count is inconsistent between Results (15) and Methods (14 effective) in the version of record.
